title: Effects of a centralized, interdisciplinary care for patients with pancreatic cancer – a prospective before-and-after study at Heidelberg University Hospital
summary:
This study aims to improve the care of patients diagnosed with a malignant tumor of the pancreas.
From the initial suspicion of a malignant pancreatic disease, through confirmation of the diagnosis, to the initiation of necessary therapy, varying amounts of time can pass—depending on the patient’s referral pathway and level of access to care.
Given the prognosis of this disease, it is advisable to keep the time window from diagnosis to the start of therapy as short as possible.
Studies have shown that delays in therapy increase mortality and reduce the chances of survival without recurrence of the disease.
Therefore, with this study, we aim to demonstrate that bringing together the various medical specialties required for treatment in one physical location improves interdepartmental communication and leads to a more timely initiation of therapy.
The departments necessary for your treatment include surgery, oncology, and radiology at Heidelberg University Hospital.
Through close collaboration of the teams in a single location, we hope to reduce waiting times for appointments and thus the start of treatment, ultimately improving patient care.
The goal is to increase the chances of survival without recurrence and reduce mortality in the future.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with an already initiated systemic therapy as well as therapy-naive patients
Diagnosis of recurrence or metastases in patients with pancreatic cancer
Exclusion criteria:
Inability to provide informed consent
Benign diseases of the pancreas
Patients with neuroendocrine tumors of the pancreas
Ongoing therapy already taking place at Heidelberg University Hospital
